parts.note: super is a colloquial word for excellent
a visor is a shield for the eyes, as on a helmet or cap

explanation.surface: A police inspector has a fine protective shield.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's on 'Inspector' stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An overseer who checks others' work is an inspector of sorts, a synonym in the workplace sense.

explanation.surface: Someone lands an illegal low punch in a boxing match.
explanation.definitionFit: To sock someone is to punch them; a sock is also worn on the foot, far beneath the waistband.

explanation.surface: A short instruction to reverse a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To punt is to bet on, or back, a horse; a punt is also a flat-bottomed river craft poled along.

clue.text: Repentant with French way three-quarters complete

parts.note: rue is the French word for a street

indicators.note: keeping three of the four letters means the last one is dropped

parts.note: complete means full

explanation.surface: A penitent figure who has walked most of a road in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three-quarters' drops the final L from FULL, leaving FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling regret and sorrow for a wrong is being repentant, a close synonym.

clue.text: Over the moon? Much farther than that

definitions.text: Over the moon? Much farther than that

parts.words: Over the moon? Much farther than that
parts.note: a phrase for blissful happiness that literally places someone well beyond the moon, in the highest of the heavens

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a rocket flies past the moon and is told it goes much further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over the moon' is the idiom for delighted; the idiom asked for describes a joy so great it is located even further away, in the uppermost heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: Being blissfully happy is expressed by both idioms, the second one even stronger than delight.

clue.text: Loud protest from one taking over?

explanation.surface: Uproar from someone seizing control of a business.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the word as a verb, out-cry: to shout louder than another and so take over the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A public clamour of objection is an outcry; to outcry someone is to overpower their voice by shouting louder.

indicators.note: almost means the word falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: spare means surplus or superfluous

explanation.surface: An unnecessary container that is nearly redundant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last letter E from SPARE.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box, especially in practice bouts.

clue.text: Very heavy stroke heaped above waterway

indicators.note: in a down clue, above means the first part comes over the second

parts.note: heaped means piled up
a river is a natural waterway

explanation.surface: A massive blow struck over a pile of stuff by a canal.
explanation.definitionFit: A forceful hit or punch is called by this name, after the machine that drives posts into the ground.

parts.note: suggests a repeat purchase, but means put into order a second time

explanation.surface: A customer asks whether more stock has been requested.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordered again means sorted into a new order, which is to change the arrangement.

clue.text: Do canteens serve up liquid produced from a vapour?

indicators.note: serve up suggests the letters are dished out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A question about whether works canteens dish out water from steam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serve up' rearranges the letters of DO CANTEENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Condensation is gas cooling into liquid, and the liquid formed is the condensate.

indicators.note: in someone's clutches means held inside, so the letters sit within the word coalman's

explanation.surface: A woman caught in the grasp of the coal delivery man.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma is a woman's first name, crosswords' usual 'lady' convention.

parts.note: out can mean knocked unconscious, and a patient is a person at hospital

explanation.surface: Someone out cold being taken into hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a comatose patient; the answer is in fact someone who attends a clinic without staying overnight.
explanation.definitionFit: A person treated at a clinic without being admitted to a ward is a non-resident hospital visitor.

explanation.surface: A worn arrow on a meter or gauge.
explanation.definitionFit: Previously owned goods are second-hand; the thin needle counting seconds on a clock face is the second hand.

parts.note: reads as bouts of trembling, but also as containers, the holders for arrows being a second sense of the same word

explanation.surface: Instances of nervous trembling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both trembles and archers' arrow holders, cases in the container sense.

parts.note: persons of note look like celebrities but are musicians, playing notes

explanation.surface: Four famous people.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of four musicians or singers playing together is a quartet.

clue.text: Compiled a sitcom relating to part of the body

definitions.text: relating to part of the body

indicators.note: compiled means put together, so the letters of a sitcom are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wrote a television comedy about anatomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compiled' rearranges the letters of A SITCOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Somatic means bodily, concerning the physical frame rather than the mind.

clue.text: Fashionable new flues being of service

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, hence fashionable or socially acceptable

indicators.note: new indicates the letters of flues are made over afresh

explanation.surface: Trendy newly installed chimney pipes prove handy.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is an old British label for what is socially acceptable, hence fashionable; 'new' is the anagram signal on the chimney pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something helpful or practical is of service.

clue.text: That one with the German over there

parts.note: yon is an old word meaning that or that one
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Pointing out a particular person standing beside a German.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is an old word meaning at that distant place.

parts.note: alludes to the proverb that calls putting things off the thief of time

explanation.surface: A burglar who arrives at just the right moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Timely here means 'of time', echoing Edward Young's saying that delaying is the thief of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaying tasks steals time, as the proverb says.

indicators.note: becoming means turning into, so the letters of I tried change into something else

explanation.surface: Someone attempted to grow neater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' rearranges the letters of I TRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidier is the comparative of tidy, meaning neater or more orderly.

explanation.surface: Turn up once the loaf has proved.
explanation.definitionFit: To roll up is to arrive casually; a roll, a small bread, that has risen is a roll up.

parts.note: tricky suggests difficult, but in card games it refers to tricks: a bid to win none of them

explanation.surface: Asking whether a decision is an easy one.
explanation.walkthrough: In whist-type games such as solo, this bid undertakes to take no tricks at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A card-game declaration promising to win no tricks is literally a no-trick call.

explanation.surface: A brief two-word description of a short period.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute, said my-NEWT, means tiny; a minute, said MIN-it, is sixty seconds.

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters of motet are rearranged

parts.note: IC is 99 in Roman numerals, 100 less 1

explanation.surface: A symbolic choral piece written as opus 99.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges MOTET into TOTEM, followed by IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Totemic means serving as a symbol or emblem.

parts.note: PM looks like the Prime Minister, but afternoon time is a former morning

explanation.surface: An assessment set for the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: PM, the afternoon, comes after AM, so it is an ex-AM.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a formal test.

explanation.surface: A leaning that someone has detected in timber.
explanation.walkthrough: In bowls, the balls are called woods, and their weighting makes them curve.
explanation.definitionFit: A bias is a leaning or prejudice; in lawn bowls the woods carry a weighting causing them to curve.

parts.note: O, the zero shape, means nothing or no
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A grocer has no facts about a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogen is a variety of small sweet green-fleshed melon from Israel.

clue.text: Supporting lecturer inside who is adding taste

indicators.note: inside tells us one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: supporting means favouring or backing

explanation.surface: Backing a teacher who seasons food.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasoning food to give it more savour is flavouring it.

clue.text: Fuss when sly person gets round

parts.note: tod is a dialect name for a fox, a byword for slyness
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Commotion as a cunning character goes around.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a commotion or fuss.

clue.text: Public have three months free hunting period

parts.note: open means public or accessible to all
a season is one quarter of the year

explanation.surface: Ordinary people get a quarter's free time for hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: The stretch when game may legally be shot is the open season, and loosely any time of unrestricted attack.
